title: mapwright: keep or redo the three example maps

questions.title: Life-like map: Belisa coast
questions.question: Should the Belisa coast map stay as the life-like example for a studyquest overworld?
questions.background: An invented world (seed 4242) and a zoomed child region of it, drawn in the topographic style. Every check passed (15 pass, OCR skipped: no tesseract). Files: D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/life-like/region-life-like.png and .svg, the whole world D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/life-like/world-life-like.png (atlas style), recipes in D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/life-like/world and D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/life-like/region.
questions.why: This becomes the example the docs and the studyquest plugin point to for a realistic overworld.
look_for: Does the coast, the mountain block and the rivers look believable?
Are the town names readable at this size?
Is a long thin peninsula a good overworld for a kid's game?

media.alt: Topographic map of the Belisa coast
Atlas map of the whole world, seed 4242

options.label: Keep it as the example map
Redo it (say what to change in the note)

guess.why: Passes every bar and reads clearly; the narrow peninsula gives a natural travel line.

questions.title: Fantasy maps: dungeon and battle map
questions.question: Should the Sunken Vault dungeon and the Ruined Watchpost battle map stay as the fantasy examples?
questions.background: A lock-and-key dungeon (seed 77, cyclic method: 16 rooms, one locked door, one-way doors) and a square-grid battle map (seed 31), both ink-and-parchment. All checks passed (dungeon 20, battle 12; OCR skipped). A route from the entrance to the goal is in D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/fantasy/dungeon-path/path.svg (27 steps). Files: D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/fantasy/dungeon-fantasy.png, D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/fantasy/battle-fantasy.png (and .svg); the plain grid images for virtual tabletops are map.png in D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/fantasy/dungeon and D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/fantasy/battle.
questions.why: These become the examples for ludowright level design and the engine plugins (Universal VTT export works on both).
look_for: Dungeon: are the key, lock and goal symbols clear without a legend?
Battle map: it is sparse (two ruins, rocks, trees); is that enough to fight over?

options.label: Keep it as the example map
Redo it (say what to change in the note)

guess.why: The dungeon is good but the battle map looks thin and has no legend; I would keep the dungeon and redo the battle map with more cover.

questions.title: Sci-fi maps: Khura subsector and Raakhiki system
questions.question: Should the Khura subsector and the Raakhiki star system stay as the sci-fi examples?
questions.background: A hex subsector (seed 2077: 42 worlds, 58 jump-2 routes, one connected network) and a G-star system (seed 2077: 5 planets, 3 moons), star-chart style. All checks passed (sector 7, system 9; OCR skipped). Files: D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/sci-fi/sector-sci-fi.png, D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/sci-fi/system-sci-fi.png (and .svg); recipes and the T5 tab file in D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/sci-fi/sector and D:/m4bwa/Claude/Projects/Ai/mapwright-lab/step-e/sci-fi/system.
questions.why: These become the examples for a sci-fi game's star map.
look_for: Sector: are names and routes readable?
System: the legend mentions a green habitable zone that the schematic view does not draw, and no planet sits inside the zone; does that matter for an example?

options.label: Keep it as the example map
Redo it (say what to change in the note)

guess.why: Both read well; the habitable-zone legend gap is a code fix, not a reason to redo the map.
